content: The Chelmsford Royal Commission, chaired by Justice John Patrick Slattery, was established between 1988 and 1990 by the New South Wales (NSW) state government to investigate mental health services in the region. These groups urged the newly-elected Health Minister to fulfill his promise of initiating a Royal Commission. Initially, the commission was intended to focus on psychosurgery practices at the NSW Neuropsychiatric Institute. However, due to mounting media scrutiny, the investigation shifted its focus to Deep Sleep Therapy, a controversial treatment method associated with Dr. Harry R. Bailey. Dr. Bailey served as the director of the Neuropsychiatric Institute from 1963 to 1979 and later led the Chelmsford Private Hospital, a psychiatric facility in Sydney. The public's growing concern over these practices led to the commission changing its official title from Royal Commission into Mental Health Services to Royal Commission into Deep Sleep Therapy. Dr. Bailey, facing ongoing investigations into his medical practices, died by suicide in September 1985. In his suicide note, he wrote: Let it be known that the Scientologists and the forces of madness have won.
